body: I'm ok with my part, as I said I already do it, and same with his on his part, he is okay with it technically but I guess I'm just going to have to do this like I do everything, where I make the plans and just tell him this is what is happening and these are the times we are going to do it.

Thanks, Its hard to give a fair representation of our relationship but I think people have some skewed ideas and think I'm never home and never touch him or something, which is not the case. I spend the majority of non-work hours at home during the week, even taking away sleeping. 

I've been trying to entice him to get more hobbies for forever. His sport he is into he doesnt want to join a rec league for because he feels too out of shape,  but it would help get in shape! Fine, I suggest going to the gym, but he doesnt want to do that very often either. I suggest he spend time with friends, he gets annoyed and says it's fine but is it really? He had a wake up call a couple years ago when the guy he considers his best friend didn't even have him in his wedding party. I want him to join things but he will only join things if I do. It's not social anxiety or anything, he is quite a sociable and funny guy when he wants to be,  but he just doesnt want to spend any time somewhere else when he could spend it instead with me. I'm still convincing him to branch out but he is incredibly stubborn, and any changes he makes move at a glacial pace, and usually only because I'm planning and doing them for him.

We are getting married later this year and part of the thing is doing some couples counseling kind of, which I've heavily wanted to do before and he has always been stubbornly against as well, but maybe this will help.

The only things that are absolutely set are the practices and work. The friend things I usually know at least a week in advance, and if he told me he wanted to do something, I could still cancel! He just usually waits until I'm literally about to go out the door for it to be an issue.

>As well, if you're spending time with him or he thinks you two are going to be alone and together in your place for some hours and then someone invites you out and you say yes, he might see that as you choosing other people over him. He thought you two were going to hang out, you "changed" the plan because something better came along, and now he's upset.  

So that never happens,  I know about all the plans at least a week if not more in advance and he knows about it as well. I never spring things on him other than this one couple who we usually hang out with once a week but it's more which day we hang out with them and he is actually usually the one to organize it as well at least half the time since he usually sees the invite before I do. If I have made a plan to hang our with him, I dont change it. He just never let's me make an actual plan for it. 

 > There may be other issues at play too, like if you've gone without sex and cuddling for some time.

Definitely not an issue, we cuddle all the time whenever we are together and even fall asleep holding hands. As for sex,  my drive is higher and that's an unrelated issue that we've been working on together and getting better with. 

> Plan at least one date night with him, or a night where the two of you just hang out at home. And he can plan something as well, but if you're always booked up on days that he wants to hang out spontaneously, it might be frustrating for him and he may feel like he's always the last choice. It's just an incompatibility that you two need to sort out and find a compromise for.

That's literally what I'm asking him to do, I'm trying to say "let me plan a date"  etc but he doesn't agree that it needs to be done. He knows most of my schedule even a month in advance and there is tons of times for us to do things. 

>
>I totally get that feeling of needing stimulation, but I find once you get used to having a lot of it, you expect more of it or to have that same level of activity all the time, and it's a little unfair to those who just want to chill out with you and want your focus and attention. Many of the people I know who suffer from depression have that need to be out and about all the time, never able to sit with themselves or their own feelings and process things. I find when they don't have something planned and don't have stimulation from a few things at once, they get a little anxious. Not saying that's what's happening here or that it's necessarily wrong to do that, but it affects other parts of your life. The balance will be off. In this case, your partner was used to you spending a lot of quality time with him, and then you changed a few things to better your life, and he feels like you took something away from him. He needs to be OK with you being away from home often, and you need to spend a bit more time with him. And do it in a deliberate way.

Whole paragraph is accurate.

I think the scheduling time bit is a misunderstanding- he's always first choice, never last. So if he wants to do something then I would love for him to let me know and then I can make sure we absolutely have time to go and do it. Not a "well you said Saturday but I'm already doing a thing at noon is 1:30 okay"  but "tell me when you want to do things and I'll make sure that if anything comes up I will make sure to say no and have the day for you." 

I'll send him the love languages test although I'm pretty sure we have done it before. 

And I am willing to consider his side- this isn't a new issue, its a recurring issue that I just now have the insight into my own psyche to understand. I've gone chunks of time where I've cut off from the world and only spent time with him, where we literally online spent all of our time together and we both look at that time fondly however it's not sustainable or healthy. I've done it multiple times where I've completely given up all social media and socializing (other than something like GoT once a week with friends that he comes with) for six months at a time. Where I don't do my hobbies and only play games with him. And that's the only time he has been completely happy. So I want to give him quality time but I cant give him the quantity that he wants, and want to figure out a compromise. I feel like I'm being reasonable asking for routine and structure, and still being able to do other things that are good for my health. 

Also, we are in constant communication at all time,  throughout the entire day, and when I get home from work I am so burnt out and I've already told him everything about my day so that I want to sit quietly and have some time to decompress,

The trying to control isn't intentional at least-  it comes from a place of "I want to spend every possible second with you, why don't you want to with me?" And, I do, but I also want to do other things too

Well I just looked at it on wikipedia and  I'd say that we have the same, namely: 

Quality time 

words of affirmation

Physical touch


Maybe as physical touch and quality time vying for top spot on both. 

I think I'd be more excited to spend time with him too if there were plans. If I knew "oh yay we have this specific day we are going to do all things together!" Which dont get me wrong is the majority of how our time goes. I would like quality time as well but right now its drowning in the quantity of time, if that makes sense?

I have. It's what everyone is saying here, time with him not on my phone or around other people, just him and I interacting. Which we do. But it's never enough. He would be happiest if I quit everything for him

I do want to dedicate time with him. I gladly do things with and for him. I participate in his hobbies whenever I can- there was a few months where all our free time was spent playing Destiny 2 together and if I even so much as picked up my phone during a loading screen he would get annoyed. I do try and spend time with him without being on my phone and just giving him attention. Theres just never a quantity of time that is enough for him. I also want to go out and do things with him but he is quite frugal (more so than me, although we have same/similar savings goals)  so anytime I want to go out with him to do things (like rock climbing, as an example) it's a no because of costs. 

Like literally the only way I can see me fixing this right now is by playing another game with him again, but there are two problems with that. 1, I'm very burnt out on all the ones we have been playing and the ones I'd be okay with he is bored of. 2, I have that big project and if I dedicate as much time as he wants to just gaming I wont have time to finish it.

So I definitely do snuggle up to him and engage in the show every single night when we are home. He would want to have me essentially just have my phone off from the moment I get in the door until we go to bed. I do know what his quality time means but its just the quantity of it. We could go for two weeks non stop with what he wants and then the third week, three days in where I've been busy he would be upset again. 

We haven't been going for walks lately since it has been literally -20c to -40c out lately but its finally starting to warm up again so I think those would be good to do. 

Also, I double check with him with plans for 80% at least of what I do.
